paragraphs.source_en: By the eighth day of the fifth month of Tenshō 15, Toyotomi Hideyoshi's campaign to conquer Kyushu was effectively over. Shimazu Yoshihisa came to Taiheiji Temple in Satsuma to pay homage to Hideyoshi.

units.source_en: By the eighth day of the fifth month of Tenshō 15, Toyotomi Hideyoshi's campaign to conquer Kyushu was effectively over.
units.source_zh: 天正十五年五月初八，丰臣秀吉征伐九州的战事实际已经结束。

units.source_en: Shimazu Yoshihisa came to Taiheiji Temple in Satsuma to pay homage to Hideyoshi.
units.source_zh: 岛津义久来到萨摩的太平寺拜见秀吉。

paragraphs.source_zh: 天正十五年五月初八，丰臣秀吉征伐九州的战事实际已经结束。岛津义久来到萨摩的太平寺拜见秀吉。

paragraphs.source_en: When he set out from Osaka Castle on the first day of the third month, imperial envoys, princes, and court nobles saw him off; he traveled only some forty or fifty li a day, taking the journey at his leisure. His attire was extraordinary as well: scarlet armor, a kuwagata-crested helmet, a robe of red brocade, and even a false mustache—an astonishing spectacle.

units.source_en: When he set out from Osaka Castle on the first day of the third month, imperial envoys, princes, and court nobles saw him off; he traveled only some forty or fifty li a day, taking the journey at his leisure.
units.source_zh: 三月初一他从大坂城出发时，由敕使、亲王公卿等相送，一天大约只走四五十里路，很是轻松。

units.source_en: His attire was extraordinary as well: scarlet armor, a kuwagata-crested helmet, a robe of red brocade, and even a false mustache—an astonishing spectacle.
units.source_zh: 他的装束也很奇怪，着绯色铠，戴锹形盔，披赤锦袍，还挂着假髭，这种装扮让人大吃一惊。

paragraphs.source_zh: 三月初一他从大坂城出发时，由敕使、亲王公卿等相送，一天大约只走四五十里路，很是轻松。他的装束也很奇怪，着绯色铠，戴锹形盔，披赤锦袍，还挂着假髭，这种装扮让人大吃一惊。

paragraphs.source_en: On the twenty-sixth he reached Akamagaseki, where he paid homage to the image of Emperor Antoku at Amidaji Temple and held a splendid poetry gathering.

units.source_en: On the twenty-sixth he reached Akamagaseki, where he paid homage to the image of Emperor Antoku at Amidaji Temple and held a splendid poetry gathering.
units.source_zh: 二十六日抵达赤间关，在此参拜了阿弥陀寺里的安德天皇像，还举行了盛大的歌会。

paragraphs.source_zh: 二十六日抵达赤间关，在此参拜了阿弥陀寺里的安德天皇像，还举行了盛大的歌会。

paragraphs.source_en: Fallen blossoms drift away upon the stream; a timeworn sleeve brushes the清 wind.

units.source_en: Fallen blossoms drift away upon the stream; a timeworn sleeve brushes the清 wind.
units.source_zh: 落花逐水去，古袖拂清风。

paragraphs.source_zh: 落花逐水去，古袖拂清风。

paragraphs.source_en: While sending Kōzan Ōgo, a monk of Mount Koya, Isshiki Akihide, an envoy of the former shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki, and others to urge surrender, he secretly had Kyushu's great merchant houses employ every possible means to sow dissension. He wanted the world to see that the enemy collapsed in fear the moment Hideyoshi arrived. Thus, until the Shimazu showed some sign of surrender, Hideyoshi made his progress all the more leisurely and kept his host moving at an even slower pace.

units.source_en: While sending Kōzan Ōgo, a monk of Mount Koya, Isshiki Akihide, an envoy of the former shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki, and others to urge surrender, he secretly had Kyushu's great merchant houses employ every possible means to sow dissension.
units.source_zh: 他一面派遣高野山的僧侣兴山应其、前将军足利义昭的使者一色昭秀等去劝降，背地里又令九州的大商家千方百计使离间计。

units.source_en: He wanted the world to see that the enemy collapsed in fear the moment Hideyoshi arrived.
units.source_zh: 他想让世人看到，秀吉一到，对方望风而溃。

units.source_en: Thus, until the Shimazu showed some sign of surrender, Hideyoshi made his progress all the more leisurely and kept his host moving at an even slower pace.
units.source_zh: 所以，在岛津还未表现出投降之意时，秀吉的巡游更是悠闲，队伍更是迟迟不进。

paragraphs.source_zh: 他一面派遣高野山的僧侣兴山应其、前将军足利义昭的使者一色昭秀等去劝降，背地里又令九州的大商家千方百计使离间计。他想让世人看到，秀吉一到，对方望风而溃。所以，在岛津还未表现出投降之意时，秀吉的巡游更是悠闲，队伍更是迟迟不进。

paragraphs.source_en: On the sixty-third day after leaving Osaka—the third day of the fifth month—Hideyoshi reached Taiheiji in Satsuma, and the Shimazu declared their intention to surrender. From the day Hideyoshi set forth, the Shimazu had held out for barely more than sixty days.

units.source_en: On the sixty-third day after leaving Osaka—the third day of the fifth month—Hideyoshi reached Taiheiji in Satsuma, and the Shimazu declared their intention to surrender.
units.source_zh: 秀吉自大坂出发后的第六十三日——五月初三，到了萨摩的太平寺时，岛津表示要投降。

units.source_en: From the day Hideyoshi set forth, the Shimazu had held out for barely more than sixty days.
units.source_zh: 自秀吉出发时始，岛津不过坚持抵抗了六十多日。

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀吉自大坂出发后的第六十三日——五月初三，到了萨摩的太平寺时，岛津表示要投降。自秀吉出发时始，岛津不过坚持抵抗了六十多日。

paragraphs.source_en: Naturally, his clansmen fiercely opposed surrender. They wanted to seal off Kagoshima and share its fate. But Yoshihisa was not foolish enough to do anything so senseless. Yet precisely because of that, he now felt sorrow, regret, self-mockery, and rage.

units.source_en: Naturally, his clansmen fiercely opposed surrender.
units.source_zh: 当然，家中人强烈反对投降。

units.source_en: They wanted to seal off Kagoshima and share its fate.

ja.t: にしようとしたのである。

units.source_zh: 他们想封锁鹿儿岛，与此地共存亡。

units.source_en: But Yoshihisa was not foolish enough to do anything so senseless.
units.source_zh: 但义久还没愚昧到做这种傻事。

units.source_en: Yet precisely because of that, he now felt sorrow, regret, self-mockery, and rage.

ja.t: しかし、それだからこそ、

units.source_zh: 但正是因此，他才有今天的悲哀、悔恨、自嘲、愤怒。

paragraphs.source_zh: 当然，家中人强烈反对投降。他们想封锁鹿儿岛，与此地共存亡。但义久还没愚昧到做这种傻事。但正是因此，他才有今天的悲哀、悔恨、自嘲、愤怒。

paragraphs.source_en: Yoshihisa left Kagoshima and, on the way, stopped at Sessōin in Ijūin Village, his mother's family temple, where he shaved his head. Of course, he did not imagine that this would settle everything. He had resolved that if Hideyoshi's demands proved too harsh, he would commit seppuku at once. Accordingly, he brought not a single attendant and came alone to the entrance of Hideyoshi's headquarters tent.

units.source_en: Yoshihisa left Kagoshima and, on the way, stopped at Sessōin in Ijūin Village, his mother's family temple, where he shaved his head.
units.source_zh: 义久从鹿儿岛启程，中途曾顺道去了生母家庙伊集院村的雪窗院落发。

units.source_en: Of course, he did not imagine that this would settle everything.

ja.t: むろん、それですべてが

units.source_zh: 当然，他并不认为这就万事大吉了。

units.source_en: He had resolved that if Hideyoshi's demands proved too harsh, he would commit seppuku at once.
units.source_zh: 他决心已定，只要秀吉提出的要求过苛，他就马上切腹。

units.source_en: Accordingly, he brought not a single attendant and came alone to the entrance of Hideyoshi's headquarters tent.
units.source_zh: 因此，他没有带一个侍从，独自来到秀吉本阵帐外。

paragraphs.source_zh: 义久从鹿儿岛启程，中途曾顺道去了生母家庙伊集院村的雪窗院落发。当然，他并不认为这就万事大吉了。他决心已定，只要秀吉提出的要求过苛，他就马上切腹。因此，他没有带一个侍从，独自来到秀吉本阵帐外。

paragraphs.source_en: Within the tent there was utter silence. Yoshihisa supposed that Hideyoshi and his staff were waiting in stern formation to display their authority. But what he found was entirely unexpected: there were no pages or other warriors inside, only a tea master whose head, like his own, was shaven, waiting quietly.

units.source_en: Within the tent there was utter silence.
units.source_zh: 帐内寂然无声。

units.source_en: Yoshihisa supposed that Hideyoshi and his staff were waiting in stern formation to display their authority.
units.source_zh: 义久以为，秀吉与幕僚正森然以待，以显示威仪。

units.source_en: But what he found was entirely unexpected: there were no pages or other warriors inside, only a tea master whose head, like his own, was shaven, waiting quietly.
units.source_zh: 可事情出乎他的意料，帐中，近侍都不在，也无其他武士，只有一个和他一样光着头的茶人，静静待在那里。

paragraphs.source_zh: 帐内寂然无声。义久以为，秀吉与幕僚正森然以待，以显示威仪。可事情出乎他的意料，帐中，近侍都不在，也无其他武士，只有一个和他一样光着头的茶人，静静待在那里。

paragraphs.source_en: “Ha! Shimazu, what are you still hesitating for? Come in at once!” Hideyoshi called loudly.

units.source_en: “Ha! Shimazu, what are you still hesitating for?

ja.t: をまだためらっておる？

units.source_zh: “哈哈，岛津啊，你还犹豫什么？

paragraphs.source_zh: “哈哈，岛津啊，你还犹豫什么？快进来！”秀吉大声道。

paragraphs.source_en: At those words, Yoshihisa suddenly felt the blood surge to his head. The humiliation of defeat swelled within him. He removed both his swords, went inside, and sat down.

units.source_en: At those words, Yoshihisa suddenly felt the blood surge to his head.
units.source_zh: 义久听了，猛然脑袋发涨。

units.source_en: The humiliation of defeat swelled within him.
units.source_zh: 战败的耻辱感在他心里膨胀。

units.source_en: He removed both his swords, went inside, and sat down.
units.source_zh: 他解下大小佩刀，到里面坐下。

paragraphs.source_zh: 义久听了，猛然脑袋发涨。战败的耻辱感在他心里膨胀。他解下大小佩刀，到里面坐下。

paragraphs.source_en: “How did Shimazu Yoshihisa come to be a shaven-headed monk?” Hideyoshi smiled, resting a thin, sinewy hand on the armrest. He looked entirely at ease. “I took the Shimazu for country folk, but I see you have thought matters through with remarkable care. May is terribly hot here!”

units.source_en: “How did Shimazu Yoshihisa come to be a shaven-headed monk?”
units.source_zh: “岛津义久怎么成了落发的和尚？”

units.source_en: Hideyoshi smiled, resting a thin, sinewy hand on the armrest. He looked entirely at ease. “I took the Shimazu for country folk, but I see you have thought matters through with remarkable care.

paragraphs.source_zh: “岛津义久怎么成了落发的和尚？”秀吉微笑，把细瘦的手支在扶几上，他看起来很是轻松，“我以为岛津是乡下人，没想到考虑得这般周到。这里的五月真热啊！”

paragraphs.source_en: “Yes.”

units.source_en: “Yes.”

paragraphs.source_en: “Master, give Shimazu a round fan. It is too hot to talk like this.”

units.source_en: “Master, give Shimazu a round fan. It is too hot to talk like this.”

paragraphs.source_en: Yoshihisa felt Hideyoshi's ill-intentioned gaze appraising him. He abruptly straightened and said, “As you can see, my lord, I have shaved my head. What are the terms of peace? Name them.”

units.source_en: Yoshihisa felt Hideyoshi's ill-intentioned gaze appraising him. He abruptly straightened and said, “As you can see, my lord, I have shaved my head.
units.source_zh: 义久感觉到秀吉不怀好意的目光在打量他，他猛然挺直上身，道：“正如大人所见，我把头发剃光了。

units.source_en: What are the terms of peace?

paragraphs.source_zh: 义久感觉到秀吉不怀好意的目光在打量他，他猛然挺直上身，道：“正如大人所见，我把头发剃光了。议和有何条件？说吧。”

paragraphs.source_en: “Ha, first compose yourself. Do not be so tense. Let us begin with how you feel.”

units.source_en: “Ha, first compose yourself. Do not be so tense. Let us begin with how you feel.”
units.source_zh: “哈哈，先放松放松，莫要那么紧张，先谈谈你的心境吧。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “哈哈，先放松放松，莫要那么紧张，先谈谈你的心境吧。”

paragraphs.source_en: “How it feels to have lost?”

units.source_en: “How it feels to have lost?”
units.source_zh: “吃了败仗的心境？”

paragraphs.source_zh: “吃了败仗的心境？”

paragraphs.source_en: “I want to know why you clung so stubbornly to a futile war.”

units.source_en: “I want to know why you clung so stubbornly to a futile war.”
units.source_zh: “我想知，你怎会对无益的战事那么执著？”

paragraphs.source_zh: “我想知，你怎会对无益的战事那么执著？”

paragraphs.source_en: “Ha! You forget that I am now the kampaku, Shimazu. Had I been merely the Governor of Chikuzen, you would have had a worthy adversary—but I am not!”

units.source_en: “Ha! You forget that I am now the kampaku, Shimazu.
units.source_zh: “哈哈，你忘了我已是关白，岛津。

units.source_en: Had I been merely the Governor of Chikuzen, you would have had a worthy adversary—but I am not!”
units.source_zh: 若我是筑前守，你便有了好对手，可我不是！”

paragraphs.source_zh: “哈哈，你忘了我已是关白，岛津。若我是筑前守，你便有了好对手，可我不是！”

paragraphs.source_en: “When my retainers and people saw you and your banners, my lord, they submitted one after another and abandoned me!” When Yoshihisa finished, he burst into loud laughter. paragraphs.source_en: But the laughter stopped abruptly. This was not yet the time to laugh, he thought.

units.source_en: But the laughter stopped abruptly.

paragraphs.source_en: A few days earlier, when Hideyoshi received Kōno Michisada, the retainer whom Shimazu had sent to sue for peace, he had said, “Judging by Shimazu's attitude, we shall have to make him come here himself!” His manner had been severe and admitted no argument.

units.source_en: A few days earlier, when Hideyoshi received Kōno Michisada, the retainer whom Shimazu had sent to sue for peace, he had said, “Judging by Shimazu's attitude, we shall have to make him come here himself!”

units.source_en: His manner had been severe and admitted no argument.

units.source_en: Hideyoshi suddenly leaned toward him. His voice was surprisingly soft and his manner intimate; the sharpness had vanished from his eyes, and his face was all warmth. “Shimazu, nothing could be better if your resolve is firm.”

paragraphs.source_en: Shimazu Yoshihisa felt like laughing. At first Hideyoshi had been light as the wind, and then, unable to contain himself, he had immediately revealed his true purpose. He knew he ought to express joyful gratitude, yet not the faintest smile came; he felt both bitterness and sorrow. The pressure concealed within this little man was closing in upon him, bit by bit.
